operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL and UPPER_CASE; generated SQL must double-quote them ("REGION_ID").
No spaces/mixed case in table names; all tables lowercase, all columns uppercase — case-insensitive lookup still needed.
HIRE_DATE/START_DATE/END_DATE declared `date` but stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD'; one START_DATE sample is '0000-00-00' (invalid date, parses as int? no — leading zeros).
REGION_NAME values carry trailing '\r' (e.g. 'Europe\r') — literal pool will contain CR-suffixed strings.
COMMISSION_PCT decimal(2,2) has mixed storage classes integer(0) and real(0.4,0.25) — affinity contradiction.
MANAGER_ID in employees has sample '0' (no employee 0) — dangling self-ish reference; departments.MANAGER_ID also references employees but no declared FK.
job_history PK is composite (EMPLOYEE_ID, START_DATE); EMPLOYEE_ID sample '0' has no parent in employees (dangling FK value).
All FKs point to existing, unique parents (regions, countries, departments, jobs, employees) — no missing/non-unique parents here.
Tiny tables (4–107 rows); no huge-table sampling concern.
STATE_PROVINCE has empty-string sample; POSTAL_CODE numeric-looking text.
departments.MANAGER_ID / employees.MANAGER_ID are logical FKs to employees.EMPLOYEE_ID but NOT declared — TS will not link them.
decimal(4,0)/(6,0) etc. all dispatch to Number with scale=0, precision=4/6; no crash-fallback types present.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer for all decimal columns: range [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1] for scale 0 → tiny ints, wildly implausible for IDs/salaries (e.g. EMPLOYEE_ID in [-1,1]).
Number list-range quirk (list_max overwritten to full max) means fresh draws dominate; original 5 sampled values perturbed ±1/±2.
String fuzzer for varchar: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length up to declared length; names/emails/cities become gibberish → FN on name/email/city predicates.

HIRE_DATE/START_DATE/END_DATE: declared `date`, first element '1987-06-17' not int → Date fuzzer, template %Y-%m-%d; but '0000-00-00' may parse oddly; fresh dates uniform 1800–2100 → implausible hire dates (FN on date-range queries).

FK columns (JOB_ID, DEPARTMENT_ID, COUNTRY_ID, REGION_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID) draw from parent's final values with replacement → duplicates and ties appear; good for join/group-by but may create implausible combos.
PK dedup keeps first occurrence; composite PK job_history dedup on (EMPLOYEE_ID,START_DATE) — many rows dropped since EMPLOYEE_ID range tiny.
NOT NULL/CHECK not enforced in Python; rows violating NOT NULL (e.g. LAST_NAME, EMAIL, CITY, HIRE_DATE) fail at insert and are skipped → smaller tables, possible empty tables.
Tiny original tables (4–107 rows) → TS sizes (30–2500) far exceed originals; joins produce many-to-many blowups.
No declared FK for MANAGER_ID → TS generates random manager ids unrelated to employees → FN on self-join manager queries.
COMMISSION_PCT scale=2 → range [-100,100] floats, implausible vs original 0–0.4 → FN on commission predicates.
REGION_NAME trailing '\r' in pool → string equality on region names likely fails (FP/FN).
Empty-string STATE_PROVINCE and '0' MANAGER_ID/EMPLOYEE_ID in pool seed odd literals.
